title: MOS Capacitor C-V Explorer
description: High-frequency, low-frequency, and deep-depletion capacitance-voltage curves of a metal/SiO2/p-type silicon capacitor at 300 K, with accumulation, depletion, and inversion shaded and the flat-band voltage, threshold voltage, oxide capacitance, and minimum capacitance marked. A band diagram follows a probe voltage. Sliders set the oxide thickness, substrate doping, fixed oxide charge, interface trap density, and gate work function.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: semiconductor physics
MOS capacitor
capacitance-voltage characteristics
flat-band voltage
threshold voltage
oxide charge
interface traps

educational.topic: Capacitance-voltage characteristics of the MOS capacitor
learningObjectives: Identify the accumulation, depletion, and inversion regions from the shape of a C-V curve
Extract the flat-band voltage, threshold voltage, oxide thickness, and substrate doping from a C-V curve
Diagnose fixed charge and interface traps from a parallel shift or a stretch-out of the curve
prerequisites: Band bending and the depletion approximation
MOS bias regimes, flat-band voltage, and threshold voltage

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameter sliders with a real-time C-V plot, a linked band diagram at a probe voltage, and a readout strip
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Predict-test-observe, followed by parameter extraction from a curve whose settings are hidden
assessmentOpportunities: Extract the oxide thickness from C_ox and the doping from C_min/C_ox
Tell fixed charge from interface traps using the reference curve
Explain why the high- and low-frequency curves differ only in inversion

equations: V_T = V_FB + 2 phi_F + q N_A W_dep,max / C_ox, W_dep,max = sqrt(4 eps_s phi_F / q N_A)
|Q_s| = sqrt(2 eps_s kT N_A) sqrt[(e^-u + u - 1) + (n_i/N_A)^2 (e^u - u - 1)], u = q psi_s / kT
assumptions: p-type silicon at 300 K, n_i = 9.65e9 cm^-3, E_g = 1.130 eV, chi = 4.05 eV, eps_s = 11.7 eps_0
Uniform interface trap density, neutral when the Fermi level is at midgap at the surface
Fixed charge located at the oxide-silicon interface
limitations: No quantum confinement, polysilicon depletion, or gate tunneling for thin oxides
High-frequency curve uses the fixed-inversion-charge approximation
Interface traps respond fully at low frequency and not at all at high frequency
